planted.description: Plain AddDbContext<OrdersDbContext> while Wolverine handlers inject the context. Wolverine 6 forbids service location by default, so the first ShipOrder throws InvalidServiceLocationException. Use opts.Services.AddDbContextWithWolverineIntegration<OrdersDbContext>(...) or optionsLifetime: ServiceLifetime.Singleton.

SaveChangesAsync, then bus.PublishAsync in a minimal API endpoint. AutoApplyTransactions does not apply outside a handler, so the order and the message are two transactions: a crash between them loses the message. Use IDbContextOutbox<OrdersDbContext> (PublishAsync, then SaveChangesAndFlushMessagesAsync) or InvokeAsync to a handler.

UseRabbitMq(...).AutoProvision() without UseQuorumQueues() and without publisher confirms. The transport declares classic queues and turns confirms off by default, so the durable outbox can delete a message that the broker refused. Add UseQuorumQueues() and ConfigureChannelCreation with both confirm flags.
try/catch that logs and returns. Wolverine sees a success and acks the message, so a failed ship is lost and never retried or moved to the error queue. Let the exception reach the error policy.

A handler that returns bool is not a handler in Wolverine 6 (primitive return type). InvokeAsync<bool> in OrderEndpoints.cs line 41 throws IndeterminateRoutesException. Return a record, for example StockResult(bool InStock), or call a plain service.

OnException<Exception>().RetryWithCooldown(...) retries each exception, also validation and business errors, and has no scheduled retry or error queue step. Write a policy for each exception type: transient errors with cooldown, then ScheduleRetry with jitter, then the error queue; business errors to the error queue at once (MSG-08).

IMessageBus injected into a domain service. Return OrderShipped as a cascading message from the handler instead, so that the handler stays a pure function and the message goes out with the transaction.
await Task.Delay(2000) to wait for the handler: slow and flaky. Use a tracked session: host.TrackActivity().Timeout(...).ExecuteAndWaitAsync(...) or InvokeMessageAndWaitAsync.
